title: 296: The Nazis: The Beer Hall Putsch (Part 2)

sentences.en: The judges of this state may tranquilly condemn us for our conduct at that time, but history, the goddess of a higher truth and a better legal code,
sentences.zh: 本州的法官们或许可以心安理得地因我们当时的所作所为而判决我们，但历史，这位更高真理与更优法典的女神，

sentences.en: will smile as she tears up this verdict and will acquit us all of the crime for which this verdict demands punishment.
sentences.zh: 当她撕毁这份判决书时，会报以微笑，并宣告我们所有人无罪，而这份判决书所要求的惩罚也将随之烟消云散。

sentences.en: But history will then also summon before its own tribunal those who, invested with power today, have trampled on law and justice, condemning our people to misery and ruin,
sentences.zh: 但历史届时也会将那些如今身居高位、践踏法律与正义、使我们的人民陷入苦难与毁灭的人，传唤到她自己的法庭前，

sentences.en: and who, in the hour of their country's misfortune,
sentences.zh: 而这些人，在国家遭遇不幸的时刻，

sentences.en: took more account of their own egos than of the life of the community.
sentences.zh: 比起社群的生命，他们更看重自己的私欲。

sentences.en: That was a failed postcard artist, former corporal in the Bavarian army, and leader of the Nazi party, Adolf Hitler, defending himself at his trial in the spring of 1924,
sentences.zh: 那是阿道夫·希特勒，一个失败的明信片画家、巴伐利亚军队的前下士、纳粹党的领袖，他在1924年春天的审判中为自己辩护，

sentences.en: attempting to overthrow the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 试图推翻魏玛共和国。

sentences.en: And Dominic, in the first part of our epic sweep through the rise of the Nazis, we looked at the background to the emergence of the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在我们史诗般回顾纳粹崛起的系列节目第一部分中，我们探讨了纳粹党出现的背景。

sentences.en: And the Beer Hall Putsch is a kind of famous way marker in that story, and we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 啤酒馆政变是那个故事中一个著名的里程碑，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: But before we do that, let's look at the background to the Beer Hall Putsch and to Hitler's contempt for the legal and political structure that are governing Germany at this time.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，让我们先看看啤酒馆政变的背景，以及希特勒对当时统治德国的法律和政治结构的蔑视。

sentences.en: And those structures are kind of basically summed up by that phrase,
sentences.zh: 而这些结构基本上可以用那个词来概括，

sentences.en: Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 魏玛共和国。

sentences.en: So what is the Weimar Republic?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是魏玛共和国？

sentences.en: Where's Weimar?
sentences.zh: 魏玛在哪里？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, big questions, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，这可是大问题。

sentences.en: So yes, hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 那么，是的，大家好。

sentences.en: We left Hitler last time, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们上次讲到希特勒时，他还在，对吧？

sentences.en: At the beginning of the 1920s, the head of this very small,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代初，他是这个非常小、

sentences.en: frankly, quite cranky political party in Munich, not a major national force by any means.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，相当古怪的慕尼黑政党的首领，绝非什么国家级的主要力量。

sentences.en: I mean, Hitler, a former nobody who has found his voice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希特勒，一个曾经的无名小卒，终于找到了自己的声音。

sentences.en: And I suppose, Tom, it would be fair to say that without the weakness of the Weimar Republic, there is no Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 我想，汤姆，公平地说，如果没有魏玛共和国的软弱，就不会有第三帝国。

sentences.en: There is no national socialist tyranny.
sentences.zh: 就不会有纳粹暴政。

sentences.en: There's nothing of that kind.
sentences.zh: 就不会有那种事情发生。

sentences.en: And the question that therefore hangs over this episode of the podcast is, is the failure of the Weimar Republic inevitable?
sentences.zh: 因此，萦绕在本期播客的一个问题是：魏玛共和国的失败是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: Is it doomed from the very beginning?
sentences.zh: 它从一开始就注定失败了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, one issue is that nobody really had sort of set out to create it or wanted to set it up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个问题是，根本没有人真正打算创建它，或者想要建立它。

sentences.en: So last time we talked about the end of the First World War in Germany, how it all happened so suddenly in the early days of November 1918.
sentences.zh: 所以上次我们谈到了德国第一次世界大战的结束，谈到了1918年11月初一切是如何突然发生的。

sentences.en: You know, in a matter of a handful of days, there are mutinies and rebellions and uprisings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在短短几天内，就发生了兵变、叛乱和起义。

sentences.en: The Kaiser disappears off into exile.
sentences.zh: 德皇流亡海外。

sentences.en: Their sort of governing structures seem to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 他们的治理结构似乎分崩离析。

sentences.en: And amid all this chaos, the man who is really emblematic of the Weimar Republic,
sentences.zh: 而在这一切混乱之中，那个真正象征着魏玛共和国的人，

sentences.en: Friedrich Ebert, who is the leader of the SPD, the Social Democratic Party, he basically seizes the moment to try and create a new structure.
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·艾伯特，社会民主党（SPD）的领袖，他基本上抓住了这个时机，试图建立一个新的结构。

sentences.en: And he does that, actually, not because he desperately wants to,
sentences.zh: 他这样做，实际上并非因为他迫切想要这样做，

sentences.en: Ebert was a monarchiSt.
sentences.zh: 艾伯特是个君主制拥护者。

sentences.en: He famously said to Prince Max of Baden, he hated the idea of a social and political revolution.
sentences.zh: 他曾对巴登亲王马克斯说过一句名言，他厌恶社会和政治革命的想法。

sentences.en: He said, I hate it like sin.
sentences.zh: 他说，我像厌恶罪恶一样厌恶它。

sentences.en: But also, Dominic, isn't, I mean, isn't the reason why it's in Weimar, which is the hometown of Goethe,
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，难道不是因为魏玛是歌德的故乡，

sentences.en: is that it's kind of looking back to a time when Germany was famous, not for its armies and its militarism, but for its culture, its learning, its scholarship.
sentences.zh: 所以才选择在那里，这是否意味着回望那个德国因文化、学识和学术而闻名，而非因军队和军国主义而闻名的时代？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，没错。

sentences.en: So it's looking back to the early 19th century, mid-19th century, the failed revolutions of 1848.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在回望19世纪初、19世纪中叶，以及1848年失败的革命。

sentences.en: So there's liberal tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有自由主义的传统。

sentences.en: Ebert is leader of the Social Democrats, but he is not a sort of hardcore Marxist or a hardcore revolutionary or anything of the kind.
sentences.zh: 艾伯特是社会民主党的领袖，但他并不是那种强硬的马克思主义者或激进的革命者，或者类似的人。

sentences.en: Not in any way a Führer.
sentences.zh: 绝非什么元首。

sentences.en: No, you could almost see him as a kind of German Clement Attlee, for our British listeners.
sentences.zh: 不，对于我们的英国听众来说，你几乎可以把他看作是德国版的克莱门特·艾德礼。

sentences.en: So he's very patriotic.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常爱国。

sentences.en: He's very sort of pragmatic.
sentences.zh: 他非常务实。

sentences.en: He makes an alliance with the Centre Party, which is the Catholic Party, and with the Liberals in 1918-19, and with the army, and with the army high command.
sentences.zh: 他在1918-1919年与中央党（即天主教党）、自由派以及军队和军队最高统帅部结成了联盟。

sentences.en: They all agree, listen, the threat of revolution amid the shock of defeat is so great.
sentences.zh: 他们都同意，听着，战败冲击下的革命威胁太大了。

sentences.en: We have to get this thing together, stabilise it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把这个国家整合起来，稳定局势。

sentences.en: So they meet in Weimar, which, as you say, is identified with the greatest German writer, Goethe.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在魏玛会面，正如你所说，魏玛与德国最伟大的作家歌德联系在一起。

sentences.en: And they put together a constitution for this republic.
sentences.zh: 他们为这个共和国制定了一部宪法。

sentences.en: And the constitution, it's against the backdrop of all that fighting and the Spartacist uprising, as you mentioned, Rosa Luxemburg and Marxists being shot out of hand and stuff.
sentences.zh: 而这部宪法是在所有那些战斗和斯巴达克同盟起义的背景下制定的，正如你提到的，罗莎·卢森堡和马克思主义者被草率枪决等等。

sentences.en: So Dominic, Michael Burley, another of the kind of the great British historians of this, he has a brilliant description for the mood in Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以多米尼克，迈克尔·伯利，另一位研究此领域的伟大英国历史学家，他对德国当时的情绪有一个精彩的描述。

sentences.en: He describes it as a dreadful mass sentimentality compounded of anger, fear, resentment, and self-pity.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为一种由愤怒、恐惧、怨恨和自怜交织而成的可怕的大众情感。

sentences.en: And that's a kind of brilliant way of summing up the background against which the founders of the Weimar Republic are working, and the kind of headwinds that they're moving into.
sentences.zh: 这是一种总结魏玛共和国创始人所处背景以及他们所面临的阻力的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, would those headwinds have been different in France or Britain had we lost the First World War?
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果我们输掉了第一次世界大战，法国或英国是否也会面临同样的阻力？

sentences.en: I don't think they would, actually.
sentences.zh: 我不认为会，真的。

sentences.en: I think if it had been a similarly shattering experience, that we would have had exactly the same blend, or at least a similar blend in London or in Paris.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果那是一场同样毁灭性的经历，我们在伦敦或巴黎也会有完全相同的混合情绪，或者至少是类似的混合情绪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the constitution they come up with is a little bit like Bismarck's Reich.
sentences.zh: 所以他们制定的宪法有点像俾斯麦的帝国。

sentences.en: The army and the president are sort of set slightly apart from democratic politics.
sentences.zh: 军队和总统在某种程度上被置于民主政治之外。

sentences.en: The president has this power, he has these emergency powers under what's called Article 48 of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 总统拥有这种权力，他根据宪法第48条拥有所谓的紧急权力。

sentences.en: If necessary, he can rule by decree and use the army to enforce his will.
sentences.zh: 如有必要，他可以发布法令进行统治，并利用军队来强制执行他的意志。

sentences.en: But in normal times, it will be the Reichstag, the Assembly, the Parliament,
sentences.zh: 但在正常时期，将由帝国议会、大会、议会，

sentences.en: even the majority in the Reichstag, who basically control the government.
sentences.zh: 甚至是帝国议会中的多数派，来基本控制政府。

sentences.en: Now, even at this point, because it's born in such chaos, Ebert uses this emergency power a lot.
sentences.zh: 现在，即使在这一点上，由于它诞生于如此混乱之中，艾伯特还是频繁使用这种紧急权力。

sentences.en: He uses it 136 times, in fact, always saying, there's so much disorder, I have to use it,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他使用了136次，总是说，混乱太多了，我必须使用它，

sentences.en: I have to step in, I have to use the army, which I think often he does, actually, to be quite frank, because there's so much chaos.
sentences.zh: 我必须介入，我必须动用军队，坦率地说，我认为他经常这样做，因为混乱实在太多了。

sentences.en: The problem, of course, is that that establishes a precedent, which is that basically the Reichstag and the president are set against each other,
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于这确立了一个先例，即帝国议会和总统基本上是对立的，

sentences.en: and if necessary, the president will always intervene against the wishes of democratic politicians.
sentences.zh: 如有必要，总统总是会违背民主政治家的意愿进行干预。

sentences.en: But again, that's very much an inheritance from before the war.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这在很大程度上是战前的遗产。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But the difference is that everybody thought that the Wilhelmine state was legitimate.
sentences.zh: 但不同之处在于，每个人都认为威廉时代的国家是合法的。

sentences.en: Nobody ever questioned whether the Kaiser's Reich was a legitimate expression of kind of German politics.
sentences.zh: 没有人质疑过德皇的帝国是否是德国政治的一种合法表达。

sentences.en: But the Weimar Republic is absolutely tainted from the very beginning, because, of course, it's associated with defeat.
sentences.zh: 但魏玛共和国从一开始就彻底被玷污了，因为，当然，它与战败联系在一起。

sentences.en: It's a product of defeat.
sentences.zh: 它是战败的产物。

sentences.en: So Germany has not just been defeated in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以德国不仅在第一次世界大战中战败了。

sentences.en: It's lost 13% of its national territory.
sentences.zh: 它还失去了13%的国土。

sentences.en: So Alsace, Lorraine, the Czar land becomes sort of French protectorate.
sentences.zh: 阿尔萨斯、洛林，萨尔地区变成了某种法国保护国。

sentences.en: The Rhineland is demilitarized.
sentences.zh: 莱茵兰被非军事化。

sentences.en: It's lost Western Poland, which is now part of the new Polish Republic.
sentences.zh: 它失去了西波兰，现在成了新波兰共和国的一部分。

sentences.en: The Germans feel the outrage of that.
sentences.zh: 德国人对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: They're outraged because they say the Allies are a load of hypocrites and liars, because the Allies go around talking about self-determination.
sentences.zh: 他们感到愤怒，因为他们说盟军是一群伪君子和骗子，因为盟军到处谈论民族自决。

sentences.en: But they won't let the Austrian Germans join with the other Germans in Germany.
sentences.zh: 但他们不允许奥地利德国人与德国的其他德国人合并。

sentences.en: So everybody, both in Austria and in Germany, is very upset at that.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人，无论是在奥地利还是在德国，都对此感到非常不满。

sentences.en: Because the problem for France and Britain and the Allies generally is that Germany remains potentially the richest
sentences.zh: 因为对于法国、英国和盟国来说，问题在于德国仍然是中欧潜在的最富有

sentences.en: and therefore the most militarily significant power in Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 因此也是军事上最重要的力量。

sentences.en: And so to allow a defeated Germany to end up with an even larger population would obviously totally go againSt.
sentences.zh: 所以允许一个战败的德国最终拥有更大的人口，显然会完全违背他们的意愿。

sentences.en: But of course it's hypocrisy.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这是虚伪。

sentences.en: It's pure hypocrisy.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的虚伪。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 同意。

sentences.en: I mean, that's why Austria exists to this day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是为什么奥地利至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: Austria wouldn't otherwise exiSt.
sentences.zh: 否则奥地利就不会存在了。

sentences.en: They also, as you said, that terror of sort of German power.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们也对德国的力量感到恐惧。

sentences.en: So there are strict limits on the German army and navy.
sentences.zh: 所以德国的陆军和海军受到严格限制。

sentences.en: They can't have tanks.
sentences.zh: 他们不能拥有坦克。

sentences.en: They can't have artillery.
sentences.zh: 他们不能拥有火炮。

sentences.en: They can only have 100,000 men.
sentences.zh: 他们只能拥有10万人的军队。

sentences.en: The Germans are very offended by this.
sentences.zh: 德国人对此感到非常冒犯。

sentences.en: They think it's sort of unsporting.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这有点不公平。

sentences.en: They're not being allowed to compete, as it were.
sentences.zh: 他们被剥夺了竞争的权利，可以这么说。

sentences.en: And of course, the Germans have to pay reparations.
sentences.zh: 当然，德国人还必须支付赔款。

sentences.en: They have to accept that they were guilty for the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他们必须承认他们对第一次世界大战负有罪责。

sentences.en: And they have to pay 132 billion gold marks, as well as loads of coal and hand over loads of railway engines and ships.
sentences.zh: 他们必须支付1320亿金马克，还要提供大量的煤炭，并交出大量的火车头和船只。

sentences.en: Now, some people listening to this podcast will say, well, the Germans were guilty of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 现在，一些听这个播客的人会说，好吧，德国人确实对第一次世界大战负有罪责。

sentences.en: Not all historians would say that.
sentences.zh: 并非所有历史学家都会这么说。

sentences.en: And you can bet your bottom dollar, very, very few Germans would have said that at the end of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以肯定，在第一次世界大战结束时，极少有德国人会这么说。

sentences.en: And so the only explanation, therefore, for lots of Germans, patriotic Germans, to explain what's happening is that the people who have signed up to this,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于许多爱国的德国人来说，解释正在发生的事情的唯一解释就是，那些签署了这些协议的人，

sentences.en: the Weimar politicians, are traitors.
sentences.zh: 那些魏玛政客，是叛徒。

sentences.en: They are complicit in the stab in the back.
sentences.zh: 他们是“背后捅刀子”的同谋。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Because as we said last time, a lot of Germans just didn't see the defeat coming.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们上次所说，许多德国人根本没预见到战败的到来。

sentences.en: They had been told right up to the end that they were winning the war.
sentences.zh: 直到最后，他们都被告知他们正在赢得战争。

sentences.en: And they thought when their army had launched that great offensive in 1918, this is going to win us the war.
sentences.zh: 当他们的军队在1918年发动那次大攻势时，他们以为这会为我们赢得战争。

sentences.en: Now, when it doesn't work out, they are shocked and surprised.
sentences.zh: 现在，当结果并非如此时，他们感到震惊和意外。

sentences.en: And the only explanation seems to be betrayal.
sentences.zh: 而唯一的解释似乎就是背叛。

sentences.en: A key problem in this, by the way, is that the army commanders, particularly General Ludendorff, went around telling everybody that they'd been stabbed in the back,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这里的一个关键问题是，军队指挥官，特别是鲁登道夫将军，到处告诉每个人他们被背后捅了一刀，

sentences.en: which Ludendorff must have known was a lie, you know, to cover themselves.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫一定知道这是谎言，你知道，这是为了掩盖他们自己。

sentences.en: Because they don't want to admit we were just beaten plain and square.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不想承认我们只是被彻底击败了。

sentences.en: So that's a huge issue for Weimar.
sentences.zh: 所以这对魏玛来说是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: In fact, the army generally is never very reliable in supporting it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，军队总体上从未真正可靠地支持过它。

sentences.en: So the army still keeps its old sort of Kaiser's colors of black, red, and white.
sentences.zh: 所以军队仍然保留着旧的德皇时期的黑、红、白三色旗。

sentences.en: It doesn't have the colors that we associate with Germany today, which are the Weimar colors, which are black, red, and gold.
sentences.zh: 它没有我们今天与德国联系在一起的颜色，即魏玛的颜色，黑、红、金。

sentences.en: The army is still very monarchiSt.
sentences.zh: 军队仍然非常拥护君主制。

sentences.en: The army is ignoring the Versailles Treaty.
sentences.zh: 军队无视《凡尔赛条约》。

sentences.en: You know, there are a lot of people in the army who basically can't wait to get rid of this new Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，军队里有很多人基本上迫不及待地想摆脱这个新的魏玛共和国。

sentences.en: They think it's completely illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 他们认为它完全不合法。

sentences.en: And what about the civil service?
sentences.zh: 那么公务员呢？

sentences.en: Same thing.
sentences.zh: 同样的情况。

sentences.en: Because, of course, a lot of civil servants are former military people.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，许多公务员是前军人。

sentences.en: So if you were in the army under the Kaiser, you got preference for state jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在德皇治下的军队服役，你在申请国家职位时会有优先权。

sentences.en: So even postmen, you know, state-employed, I don't know, janitors or whatever, they're often former military men.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是邮递员，你知道，国家雇佣的，我不知道，看门人什么的，他们通常都是前军人。

sentences.en: So all these people, you know, the people, the bureaucrats who are basically carrying out the Weimar Republic's instructions,
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些人，你知道，那些基本上在执行魏玛共和国指令的官僚们，

sentences.en: a lot of them think this is a load of kind of dodgy lefty traitors
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人认为这是一群卑鄙的左翼叛徒，

sentences.en: who've sold us down the river, and the whole thing is illegitimate, and I can't wait for it to go away.
sentences.zh: 他们出卖了我们，整个体制是不合法的，我迫不及待地想让它消失。

sentences.en: So the Weimar is very – has lots of governments rising and falling because it has endless coalitions.
sentences.zh: 所以魏玛非常——有很多政府起起落落，因为它有无休止的联合政府。

sentences.en: I think it has 20 different cabinets between 1919 and 1933.
sentences.zh: 我想在1919年到1933年间，它有20个不同的内阁。

sentences.en: So there's constant coalition building.
sentences.zh: 所以一直在组建联合政府。

sentences.en: But some of the biggest parties in Germany never accept the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 但德国一些最大的政党从未接受过魏玛共和国。

sentences.en: An obvious example is the communists.
sentences.zh: 一个明显的例子是共产党。

sentences.en: So the communists in the mid-1920s are getting, you know, three to four million votes.
sentences.zh: 所以20世纪20年代中期的共产党获得了，你知道，三到四百万张选票。

sentences.en: They're absolutely explicit about it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此表达得非常明确。

sentences.en: They think it's a bourgeois capitalist construct.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一个资产阶级资本主义的产物。

sentences.en: Yeah, a racket, exactly, running dogs of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 是的，一个骗局，没错，资本主义的走狗。

sentences.en: Can't wait to sweep it away.
sentences.zh: 迫不及待地想把它扫地出门。

sentences.en: But the nationalists, so that's the biggest sort of right-wing group, bigger than any other group except for the Social Democrats, they, again, are absolutely explicit.
sentences.zh: 但民族主义者，也就是最大的右翼团体，除了社会民主党之外比任何其他团体都大，他们再次表达得非常明确。

sentences.en: They say, bring back the Second Reich, bring back the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 他们说，恢复第二帝国，恢复德皇。

sentences.en: They wave the old flags.
sentences.zh: 他们挥舞着旧旗帜。

sentences.en: The biggest G's in nationalist politics, who was a press baron called Alfred Hugenberg,
sentences.zh: 民族主义政治中最重量级的人物，是一位名叫阿尔弗雷德·胡根贝格的报业大亨，

sentences.en: he's drunk very deeply of all this stuff in the 1880s and 1890s, pan-Germanism, social Darwinism, Nietzsche, Lebensraum, anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 他在19世纪80和90年代深受各种思想的影响，包括泛德意志主义、社会达尔文主义、尼采哲学、生存空间论和反犹主义。

sentences.en: He's very, very extreme.
sentences.zh: 他非常、非常极端。

sentences.en: He's always shouting about Judom, all of this business.
sentences.zh: 他总是大肆叫嚣关于犹太人的事，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So in other words, from the start, there are loads of people who want Weimar to fail.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，从一开始，就有很多人希望魏玛共和国失败。

sentences.en: And I think most historians would say,
sentences.zh: 我想大多数历史学家都会说，

sentences.en: even with a fair wind, this was a pretty fragile construction with an awful lot of people who it ought to have been able to rely on, who regard it as an affront, as tainted,
sentences.zh: 即使在顺风顺水的情况下，这依然是一个相当脆弱的架构，许多本应成为其依靠的人，却将其视为一种侮辱，一种污点，

sentences.en: and they want it to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 他们希望它分崩离析。

sentences.en: And of course, as we'll see, it never does get a fair wind.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如我们将要看到的，它从未有过顺风顺水的日子。

sentences.en: There is actually another element I thought which would interest you, Tom, because you're interested in ideas and ideology,
sentences.zh: 其实还有另一个因素，汤姆，我想你会感兴趣的，因为你对思想和意识形态很感兴趣，

sentences.en: which is the ideas and the sort of ideological and cultural swirl of the 1920s, I think, plays a part in discrediting Feimar.
sentences.zh: 那就是20世纪20年代的思想以及那种意识形态和文化的漩涡，我认为这在抹黑魏玛共和国的过程中起了一定作用。

sentences.en: Because this is an age, I mean, we talk about culture wars in, I mean, it seems ludicrous to talk about culture wars in 21st century Britain.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个时代，我的意思是，我们谈论文化战争，在21世纪的英国谈论文化战争似乎很荒谬。

sentences.en: When you think about the kind of culture wars in the, in 20s Germany,
sentences.zh: 但当你想到20年代德国的那种文化战争时，

sentences.en: everything from expressionist films and nightclubs and jazz.
sentences.zh: 从表现主义电影到夜总会和爵士乐，应有尽有。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's cabaret, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，就是歌舞表演，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the, for English speakers, that's the image of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于讲英语的人来说，这就是它的形象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or have you ever seen, there's a TV series called Babylon Berlin.
sentences.zh: 或者你看过一部叫《巴比伦柏林》的电视剧吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, big fan.
sentences.zh: 看过，我是忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: I've mentioned this before on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我之前在播客里提到过。

sentences.en: Absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 绝对精彩。

sentences.en: So it's all that sort of image that you have of kind of decadence, cross-dressing decadence in Berlin nightclubs, in cellars,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你所拥有的那种颓废形象，柏林夜总会和地下室里那种变装的颓废，

sentences.en: people listening to jazz and swing and all getting off with each other and drinking cocktails and talking to Bertolt Brecht.
sentences.zh: 人们听着爵士乐和摇摆乐，互相调情，喝着鸡尾酒，和贝托尔特·布莱希特聊天。
zh_words: 贝托尔特·布莱希特聊天

sentences.en: Apparently, apparently the favourite drink among Feimar politicians, it wasn't cocktails.
sentences.zh: 显然，显然魏玛政客们最喜欢的饮料不是鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: It was liquid yoghurt.
sentences.zh: 而是液态酸奶。

sentences.en: I read it in Michael Burley's book.
sentences.zh: 我在迈克尔·伯利的书中读到的。

sentences.en: So it must be true.
sentences.zh: 所以那一定是真的。

sentences.en: I didn't realise he was so strong on yoghurt.
sentences.zh: 我没意识到他竟然这么推崇酸奶。

sentences.en: Yeah, apparently this was the taste of Feimar.
sentences.zh: 是的，显然这就是魏玛的味道。

sentences.en: But the other thing that is happening, though, is incredible street violence.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，另一件正在发生的事情是令人难以置信的街头暴力。

sentences.en: And that presumably is an inheritance from, well, the kind of the militarised society that Germany was during the First World War,
sentences.zh: 这大概是继承自，嗯，德国在第一次世界大战期间那种军事化的社会，

sentences.en: but also this kind of, you know, the way that you have street battles raging in Berlin, in Munich, across most of the German cities.
sentences.zh: 但也包括这种，你知道，在柏林、慕尼黑以及大多数德国城市肆虐的街头巷战。

sentences.en: And the way in which it's not just the communists and the far-right parties have kind of paramilitary wings.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是共产党和极右翼政党拥有准军事组织。

sentences.en: I mean, even the major, you know, the Social Democrats do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，连主要的社会民主党也有。

sentences.en: Yeah, everybody has a paramilitary wing.
sentences.zh: 没错，每个人都有准军事组织。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So they've all, we talked a tiny bit in the first episode about the army came back, brutalised, I suppose you would say, inured to violence after the trenches.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都有，我们在第一集里稍微聊过军队回国后的情况，我想你会说他们变得残暴了，在战壕之后对暴力习以为常。

sentences.en: Of course, the war doesn't, the fighting doesn't actually end for all the Germans in November 1918.
sentences.zh: 当然，对所有德国人来说，战争并没有在1918年11月真正结束。

sentences.en: So there are still German units fighting in the utter chaos of the east, in the Baltic and so on, where everything has completely fallen apart,
sentences.zh: 所以仍有德国部队在东方的一片混乱中作战，在波罗的海等地，那里的一切都已经彻底瓦解，

sentences.en: all borders have been erased, and it's sort of, everything's up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 所有的边界都被抹去了，一切都处于待争夺的状态。

sentences.en: So this is the Fry Corps, these sort of, they're kind of freebie booty units.
sentences.zh: 这就是自由军团，这些所谓的自由雇佣兵单位。

sentences.en: You know, they're wearing German army uniforms, but they're kind of doing, going off and doing their own thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们穿着德国军装，但他们却在做着自己的事情。

sentences.en: They all come back in the 1920s, and there are, you know, hundreds of thousands of men who actually enjoyed fighting, who liked the camaraderie, the sense of belonging.
sentences.zh: 他们在20世纪20年代都回来了，有成千上万的人实际上很享受战斗，他们喜欢那种战友情谊和归属感。

sentences.en: Well, that's what the far-right is all about, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是极右翼的全部意义所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's the idea that men should get out there and fight, and that's what Darwinism tells you.
sentences.zh: 这就是男人应该走出去战斗的观念，而这正是达尔文主义告诉你的。

sentences.en: That's what nature is.
sentences.zh: 这就是自然法则。

sentences.en: So I suppose you could trace it back, couldn't you, to the sort of social Darwinism, the emphasis on struggle.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜你可以追溯到那种社会达尔文主义，对斗争的强调，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think that plays a part.
sentences.zh: 我认为这起到了一定作用。

sentences.en: Obviously, the experience of the First World War plays a massive part.
sentences.zh: 显然，第一次世界大战的经历起到了巨大的作用。

sentences.en: And those two things flow together with the experiences of all these young men into this sort of culture in the 1920s of war.
sentences.zh: 这两者与所有这些年轻人的经历汇合在一起，形成了20世纪20年代这种战争文化。

sentences.en: There's no other way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 没有别的说法了。

sentences.en: Everybody, lots of people wearing uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 每个人，很多人都穿着制服。

sentences.en: There's a constant talk of smashing, crushing, you know, all of that sort of stuff, that rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 到处都在谈论粉碎、摧毁，你知道，所有这些东西，那种言论。

sentences.en: But also the fact that on the left as well, you have the prospect of violent revolution is absolutely seen as a good.
sentences.zh: 但同样不可忽视的是，在左翼，暴力革命的前景也被绝对视为一件好事。

sentences.en: So on both sides, the extremes of both, there is an appetite for violence, not as something, you know, a regrettable necessity,
sentences.zh: 所以双方，两边的极端分子，都对暴力有着渴望，这不仅仅是，你知道，一种令人遗憾的必要手段，

sentences.en: but as something absolutely to be celebrated and stoked.
sentences.zh: 而是绝对值得庆祝和煽动的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I suppose the paramilitary leagues are the kind of institutionalization of that.
sentences.zh: 我想准军事联盟就是这种现象的制度化。

sentences.en: And as you said, each party has one.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，每个政党都有一个。

sentences.en: So there's a veterans group called the Steel Helmets.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫“钢盔团”的退伍军人组织。

sentences.en: This is massive.
sentences.zh: 规模非常大。

sentences.en: I mean, hundreds of thousands of members.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有成千上万的成员。

sentences.en: They join the Steel Helmets.
sentences.zh: 他们加入了钢盔团。

sentences.en: The Steel Helmets.
sentences.zh: 钢盔团。

sentences.en: And the Steel Helmets are the kind of the helmets that the Germans wore in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 钢盔团戴的那种头盔就是德国人在一战中戴的那种。

sentences.en: Yeah, the First World War.
sentences.zh: 是的，第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: So they're the helmets we associate with World War II, but they are wearing them at the end of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是我们与第二次世界大战联系在一起的头盔，但他们在第一次世界大战结束时就开始戴了。

sentences.en: The Steel Helmets are, I suppose, vaguely nominally neutral, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 钢盔团在名义上大概是中立的，但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: They end up being drawn to the far right.
sentences.zh: 他们最终被吸引到了极右翼。

sentences.en: The Nationalists have their fighting leagues.
sentences.zh: 民族主义者有他们的战斗联盟。

sentences.en: The Communists have what's called the Red Front Fighting League.
sentences.zh: 共产党有所谓的“红色阵线战士同盟”。

sentences.en: The Nazis, of course, have the Stormtroopers.
sentences.zh: 纳粹当然有冲锋队。

sentences.en: So they're wearing their brown shirts.
sentences.zh: 所以他们穿着棕色的衬衫。

sentences.en: The Sturmabteilung.
sentences.zh: 冲锋队。

sentences.en: I mean, initially, they were called something like the gymnastics and sports section because that was an attempt to get around the law.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最初他们被称为类似体操和体育部门的组织，因为那是为了规避法律。

sentences.en: But, you know, as you said, the Social Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如你所说，社会民主党也是如此。

sentences.en: So this is the party of Weimar, the party that was the biggest party in Germany, that has created this new republic that is kind of the left-wing party,
sentences.zh: 所以这是魏玛的政党，是德国最大的政党，创造了这个新共和国，某种程度上是左翼政党，

sentences.en: the Labour Party, if you like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，就是工党。

sentences.en: They have their own paramilitary group, the Reichsbanner, Schwarz, Rot, Gold.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的准军事组织，即“帝国旗帜黑红金”。

sentences.en: So, you know, everybody, paramilitary politics is part of Weimar from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，每个人都是如此，准军事政治从一开始就是魏玛的一部分。

sentences.en: So that's not good, is it?
sentences.zh: 那可不太妙，是吧？

sentences.en: No, that's not contributing to the stability of the system.
sentences.zh: 不，那对系统的稳定性毫无帮助。

sentences.en: And then you have the economy.
sentences.zh: 然后还有经济问题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if you'd had all that, could you still have survived?
sentences.zh: 所以如果经历了这一切，它还能存活下来吗？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许……

sentences.en: Well, because it's the economy stupid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为“笨蛋，问题在于经济”。

sentences.en: If people are rich and stable, they don't have a stake in pulling things down, do they?
sentences.zh: 如果人们富有且生活稳定，他们就不会有兴趣去推翻一切，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The less people care about politics, the better.
sentences.zh: 人们越不关心政治越好。

sentences.en: 1920s Germany is a very, very intensely politicized society.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代的德国是一个政治化程度非常、非常高的社会。

sentences.en: When people are moaning about apathy in politics, I always think, you know, be careful what you wish for, because they definitely weren't apathetic in Weimar, Germany.
sentences.zh: 当人们抱怨政治冷漠时，我总是想，你知道，小心你所祈求的，因为魏玛德国的人们绝对不冷漠。

sentences.en: And of course, one reason they're not apathetic is because they're, I mean, their living standards are being destroyed.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们不冷漠的一个原因是，我的意思是，他们的生活水平正在被摧毁。

sentences.en: So as you said in the first podcast,
sentences.zh: 所以正如你在第一个播客中所说，

sentences.en: the Germans had been borrowing a lot of money to pay for World War I.
sentences.zh: 德国人为了支付第一次世界大战的费用借了很多钱。

sentences.en: So prices had doubled between 1915.
sentences.zh: 所以物价在1915年之间翻了一番。

sentences.en: And the plan was that they would recoup this from reparations from their enemies when they won.
sentences.zh: 计划是他们获胜后从敌人的赔款中收回这些钱。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, they don't win.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他们没有赢。

sentences.en: So inflation is now absolutely through the roof.
sentences.zh: 所以现在的通货膨胀简直高得离谱。

sentences.en: They have borrowed and printed so much money that they haven't basically earned to pay for the war.
sentences.zh: 他们借了太多钱，印了太多钱，而这些钱根本不是他们赚来的，只是为了支付战争费用。

sentences.en: And now they're having to borrow it and to print it to pay for the reparations.
sentences.zh: 现在他们不得不借钱和印钱来支付赔款。

sentences.en: Because, of course, no sane government wants to raise taxes on Germans to give to the French and the British.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，没有哪个理智的政府愿意向德国人增税来交给法国人和英国人。

sentences.en: Because then you really are, you do look like a terrible traitor and November criminal and stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为那样的话，你看起来真的就像一个可怕的叛徒和“十一月罪人”之类的。

sentences.en: So to give you a sense of, I mean, inflation, it can sound so abstract.
sentences.zh: 所以为了让你有个概念，我的意思是，通货膨胀听起来可能很抽象。

sentences.en: Of course, these days, to a lot of people listening to this podcast, it won't seem abstract with how we're living with inflation at 10%.
sentences.zh: 当然，如今对于很多听这个播客的人来说，考虑到我们正生活在10%的通胀率中，这看起来并不抽象。

sentences.en: But in August 1922, to buy one US dollar, it took you 1,000 marks.
sentences.zh: 但在1922年8月，购买一美元需要1000马克。

sentences.en: By December 1922, it took you 7,000 marks.
sentences.zh: 到了1922年12月，需要7000马克。

sentences.en: Then something terrible happens to Germany.
sentences.zh: 然后德国发生了一些可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Because they're slow in repaying their reparations, the French, because they haven't been handing over all the coal they should have done,
sentences.zh: 因为他们偿还赔款的速度很慢，法国人因为他们没有按要求交出所有的煤炭，

sentences.en: occupy the main industrial region of Germany, the Ruhr.
sentences.zh: 占领了德国的主要工业区——鲁尔区。

sentences.en: They send in troops.
sentences.zh: 他们派出了军队。

sentences.en: Some of them are black colonial troops, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 其中一些是黑人殖民地军队，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Some of them are, you know, Senegalese and whatnot, African troops.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是，你知道，塞内加尔人什么的，非洲军队。

sentences.en: So that doesn't go down well with the far right.
sentences.zh: 所以这在极右翼那里并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: The Germans are extremely, extremely displeased with this.
sentences.zh: 德国人对此感到非常、非常不满。

sentences.en: There's a great boost, actually, for the Nazi party and for other far right nationalist parties.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这对纳粹党和其他极右翼民族主义政党来说是一个巨大的推动。
