sentences.zh: 但是，正如你所说，墨索里尼曾是一名记者。

sentences.en: But, as you say, Mussolini is a former journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 他曾是个无名小卒，真的。

sentences.en: He's a former nobody, really.
sentences.zh: 有点像希特勒。

sentences.en: A bit like Hitler.
sentences.zh: 也是从左翼转向了右翼。

sentences.en: Also, kind of from the left, moved to the right.
sentences.zh: 是从左翼走过来并转向了右翼。

sentences.en: Has come from the left and moved to the right.
sentences.zh: 法西斯主义、意大利法西斯主义和纳粹主义有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: Fascism, Italian fascism and Nazism have lots of similarities.
sentences.zh: 强调暴力、对议会制的不信任、受害者心态、敬礼、民族主义。

sentences.en: Emphasis on violence, distrust to parliamentarianism, sense of victimhood, salutes, nationalism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纳粹是在模仿，故意模仿意大利人的敬礼、鹅步，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the Nazis are copying, deliberately copying the salutes, the goose-stepping, all these kinds of things from the Italians.
sentences.zh: 鹰徽、旗帜，还有夺取权力的想法。

sentences.en: The eagles, the standards, also the idea of seizing power.
sentences.zh: 所以墨索里尼，我的意思是，1922年10月的向罗马进军被神话了很多。

sentences.en: So Mussolini, I mean, the march on Rome in October 1922 is much mythologized.
sentences.zh: 但最终，墨索里尼成为了“领袖”。

sentences.en: But at the end of it, Mussolini is the duche, the leader.
sentences.zh: 所以进入1923年，向柏林进军的想法在极右翼圈子里流传开来。

sentences.en: And so the idea of a march on Berlin is, I mean, that kind of idea is floating around far-right circles as you get into 1923.
sentences.zh: 所以在1923年10月，希特勒接受了《每日邮报》的采访，他在采访中说，

sentences.en: So in October 1923, Hitler actually gives an interview with, of all papers, he gives an interview to the Daily Mail, in which he says,
sentences.zh: 如果德国能有一位德国的墨索里尼，人民会跪下来崇拜他，比墨索里尼受到的崇拜还要多。

sentences.en: if a German Mussolini were given to Germany, the people would kneel down and worship him more than Mussolini has ever been worshipped.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，希特勒是否认为自己就是德国的墨索里尼？

sentences.en: At this stage, does Hitler think of himself as the German Mussolini?
sentences.zh: 这还不清楚。

sentences.en: It's not clear.
sentences.zh: 这个想法一定已经在他的脑海中成形了。

sentences.en: The idea must be taking shape in his mind.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你会说出那样的话，除非你至少有一种预感，觉得这可能会实现。

sentences.en: I don't think you'd say that without at least the kind of glimmering of a kind of hunch that it might be.
sentences.zh: 同意。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图夺取权力的道路，是一个如此奇怪而复杂的故事。

sentences.en: So the road to his attempted seizure of power, such a strange and complicated story.
sentences.zh: 慕尼黑基本上是由一个三人组统治的，一个右翼的三人组。

sentences.en: Munich is basically being run by a triumvirate, a right-wing triumvirate.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫古斯塔夫·里特·冯·卡尔的人负责政府。

sentences.en: There's a guy called Gustav Ritter von Kahr, who runs the government.
sentences.zh: 冯·赛瑟上校负责警察。

sentences.en: Colonel von Seyser runs the police.
sentences.zh: 冯·洛索将军负责军队。

sentences.en: General von Lossow runs the army.
sentences.zh: 他们统治着慕尼黑。

sentences.en: And they're running Munich.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来，到1923年底或1923年下半年，他们有自己的计划来推翻魏玛共和国，并在柏林建立一个民族主义的独裁政府。

sentences.en: And they, it seems, by the end of 1923 or the second half of 1923, they have their own plan to topple the Weimar Republic and set up a nationalist directorate in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他们对施特雷泽曼为结束恶性通货膨胀所做的让步感到愤怒。

sentences.en: They're outraged by Strasemann's concessions to end the hyperinflation.
sentences.zh: 他们参与了这个三方阴谋，一方面是希特勒和纳粹，另一方面是鲁登道夫将军。

sentences.en: They sort of get involved with this sort of three-cornered plot, with Hitler and the Nazis on the one hand, and General Ludendorff on the other.
sentences.zh: 我想这三方中的每一方都认为自己在利用其他人，并且认为自己才是最终……

sentences.en: And each of these three parties, I think, thinks they're using the others, and that they're the people who will basically...
sentences.zh: 好吧，这将是纳粹历史的一个贯穿始终的主题。

sentences.en: Well, this would be a running theme of Nazi history.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为自己在利用别人，确实如此。

sentences.en: Everybody thinks they're using everybody else, exactly.
sentences.zh: 人们在纳粹身上不断犯下的可怕错误。

sentences.en: The terrible mistake that people keep making with the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他们与柏林的军队进行了交谈，柏林的军队首脑说，不，我对此不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: They talk to the army in Berlin, and the head of the army in Berlin says, no, I'm not really up for this.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，慕尼黑的人，那些慕尼黑当局的人，他们说，好吧，你知道，我们也不会做这些事了。

sentences.en: So at that point, the guys in Munich, the Munich authority people, they say, well, you know, we're not going to do this either of them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没意义。

sentences.en: You know, no point.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒意识到他在过去一年左右的时间里煽动了一切。

sentences.en: So Hitler is sort of conscious that he stoked everything up for the last year or so.
sentences.zh: 而且人们总是对恶性通货膨胀、对法国人在鲁尔区的行为以及赔款感到愤怒，如果他不采取行动，如果他不做出那个伟大的姿态，

sentences.en: And there's always outrage about the hyperinflation and about the French and the Ruhr and reparations, that if he doesn't act, if he doesn't make the great gesture,
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处未完，根据语境补全）他就无法实现他的目标。

sentences.en: then his support people will say, well, he's all talk.
sentences.zh: 然后他的支持者会说，好吧，他只会说空话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, no action.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有实际行动。

sentences.en: And so he and Ludendorff decide, well, we'll force the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以他和鲁登道夫决定，好吧，我们要强行推进这件事。

sentences.en: They know that on the 9th of November, which is the fifth anniversary of the outbreak of the German revolution in 1918, they know that Kahr, the boss of the Munich government,
sentences.zh: 他们知道11月9日是1918年德国革命爆发五周年纪念日，他们知道卡尔，也就是慕尼黑政府的首脑，

sentences.en: basically, he's going to be addressing a meeting in the Bürgerbreue Keller in Munich, which is this sort of citizen's brewery cellar.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他要在慕尼黑的贝格勃劳凯勒啤酒馆发表演讲，那是一个市民啤酒窖。

sentences.en: And he'll be shouting about November traitors and all this sort of stuff, which he is doing.
sentences.zh: 他会大谈特谈十一月罪人什么的，他确实也这么做了。

sentences.en: Kahr is doing that, the triumvirate are there.
sentences.zh: 卡尔在做这件事，三巨头都在那里。

sentences.en: That evening, Hitler bursts in with a load of guys in brown shirts.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，希特勒带着一群穿褐色衬衫的人冲了进去。

sentences.en: It's just this stormtrooper.
sentences.zh: 那只是冲锋队。

sentences.en: It's his Kahr, a paramilitary wing, little paramilitary wing, and General Ludendorff.
sentences.zh: 那是他的卡尔，一个准军事组织，小型的准军事组织，还有鲁登道夫将军。

sentences.en: It's complete chaos in the room.
sentences.zh: 房间里一片混乱。

sentences.en: Hitler takes out his revolver, which is a browning, and he shoots a bullet into the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 希特勒掏出他的左轮手枪，那是一把勃朗宁，他朝天花板开了一枪。

sentences.en: And he says, the building is surrounded, you know, my brown shirts are here.
sentences.zh: 他说，大楼已经被包围了，我的冲锋队就在这里。

sentences.en: This is the moment.
sentences.zh: 就是这一刻。

sentences.en: He takes the triumvirate away, and he says to them, listen, I'm forcing the issue.
sentences.zh: 他把三巨头带走，对他们说，听着，我在强行推进这件事。

sentences.en: We're marching on Berlin.
sentences.zh: 我们要向柏林进军。

sentences.en: I'll be the head of the cabinet, the head of government.
sentences.zh: 我将担任内阁首脑，政府首脑。

sentences.en: Ludendorff will be the head of the army.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫将担任军队首脑。

sentences.en: And von Kahr, the guy who's been running Bavaria, you can be the head of state as a regent for the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 而冯·卡尔，那个一直管理巴伐利亚的人，你可以作为皇帝的摄政王担任国家元首。

sentences.en: You see, there's still a lot of monarchism around, actually.
sentences.zh: 你看，实际上当时还有很多君主主义者。

sentences.en: It's very interesting how long that lingers.
sentences.zh: 这种思想残留了这么久，非常有趣。

sentences.en: They all say, fine, all right, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，行，好吧，随便吧。

sentences.en: They go back in, talk to the crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们回到里面，对人群说话。

sentences.en: Hitler gives a great speech, shouts about the Berlin Jew government, says, you know, this is the end of it.
sentences.zh: 希特勒发表了一场精彩的演讲，大喊着反对柏林的犹太政府，说，你知道，这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: This very sort of, oh, stirring is not the right word with that, old Hitler.
sentences.zh: 这种非常，哦，煽动性这个词用在他身上不太合适，老希特勒。

sentences.en: Very, um...
sentences.zh: 非常，嗯……

sentences.en: Well, but in a sense, it is, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，但从某种意义上说，确实是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he does stir people up.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他确实煽动了人们。

sentences.en: He does rouse people.
sentences.zh: 他确实鼓舞了人们。

sentences.en: He does make people feel that, you know, he makes their blood race faster and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他确实让人觉得，你知道，他让他们的血液流速加快，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 说得过去。

sentences.en: Either the German revolution begins tonight, or we'll all be dead by dawn.
sentences.zh: 要么德国革命今晚开始，要么我们所有人都会在黎明前死去。

sentences.en: You know, it's quite sort of...
sentences.zh: 你知道，这相当……

sentences.en: People are all cheering and shouting.
sentences.zh: 人们都在欢呼和呐喊。

sentences.en: Then, an absolute shambles unfolds.
sentences.zh: 然后，一场彻底的混乱发生了。

sentences.en: Hitler and the Nazis go off into the city, determined to capture the barracks and the police headquarters and all this.
sentences.zh: 希特勒和纳粹分子冲进城里，决心占领军营、警察总部等等。

sentences.en: And it's a complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 结果是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: They don't actually capture any of them.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上一个也没占领。

sentences.en: None of the army, none of the police joined them at all.
sentences.zh: 军队和警察根本没有人加入他们。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in the beer cellar, total ludicrous scenes.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，回到啤酒馆，场面极其荒谬。

sentences.en: Ludendorff, who's a military man, says to the Munich Triumvirate, they say, can we go?
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫，一个军人，对慕尼黑三巨头说，他们说，我们可以走了吗？

sentences.en: You know, we give you our word.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们向你保证。

sentences.en: We'll still support the coup.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然支持政变。

sentences.en: Scout's honour.
sentences.zh: 以童子军的名义发誓。

sentences.en: And he says, oh, well, if you give me your word, of course.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，好吧，既然你们向我保证，当然可以。

sentences.en: They go.
sentences.zh: 他们走了。

sentences.en: They go and immediately repudiate the coup completely and say, we have nothing to do with this.
sentences.zh: 他们一走就立即彻底否认了政变，说，我们与此事毫无关系。

sentences.en: It's completely against our will.
sentences.zh: 这完全违背了我们的意愿。

sentences.en: They send orders to all the army units, do not listen to Hitler and the Nazis and Ludendorff at all.
sentences.zh: 他们向所有部队下令，根本不要听希特勒、纳粹和鲁登道夫的。

sentences.en: So basically, by dawn, Hitler is not dead.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，到黎明时分，希特勒没死。

sentences.en: Nobody is dead.
sentences.zh: 没有人死。

sentences.en: Hitler and co have trooped back rather miserably and forlornly to the beer cellar, where Ludendorff, looking like a fool, is waiting for them.
sentences.zh: 希特勒和同伙们垂头丧气地回到了啤酒馆，鲁登道夫看起来像个傻瓜一样在那里等着他们。

sentences.en: And they say, well, this hasn't gone well at all.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，这事一点也不顺利。

sentences.en: Do they have a drink?
sentences.zh: 他们喝了一杯吗？

sentences.en: I assume the drink's half.
sentences.zh: 我猜酒喝了一半。

sentences.en: You assume?
sentences.zh: 你猜？

sentences.en: You'd be demented not to.
sentences.zh: 不喝才不正常呢。

sentences.en: It's always wrong to do that.
sentences.zh: 那样做总是错的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You'd be mad not to, wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 不喝才疯了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, so Hitler at this stage, I think, is still drinking.
sentences.zh: 我是说，希特勒在这个阶段，我想，还在喝酒。

sentences.en: I don't think he becomes a teetotaler until after he's been in prison.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他在入狱前就戒酒了。

sentences.en: I might be wrong.
sentences.zh: 我可能错了。

sentences.en: People who know more about Hitler than I do can correct me if so.
sentences.zh: 比我更了解希特勒的人如果发现错了可以纠正我。

sentences.en: So back in the beer cellar, their supporters, you know, as dawn breaks, their supporters are kind of drifting away.
sentences.zh: 回到啤酒馆，他们的支持者，你知道，随着黎明到来，他们的支持者正在散去。

sentences.en: It's like a party that has run out of steam.
sentences.zh: 就像一场失去了动力的派对。

sentences.en: Ludendorff says, well, we have to force the issue.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫说，好吧，我们必须强行推进。

sentences.en: Let's march on the city center.
sentences.zh: 让我们向市中心进军。

sentences.en: So they do.
sentences.zh: 于是他们照做了。

sentences.en: There are about 2,000 of them by this point.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候大约有2000人。

sentences.en: They set off at midday and they're met by lines of policemen.
sentences.zh: 他们在中午出发，遇到了警察的封锁线。

sentences.en: What follows is, you know, there's a sort of confrontation, a lot of shouting, and then eventually someone starts shooting.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的是，你知道，有一种对抗，大声叫喊，然后最终有人开始开枪。

sentences.en: Of the leading Nazis, Göring is hit in the leg and Hitler falls and dislocates his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 在纳粹高层中，戈林腿部中弹，希特勒摔倒并脱臼了肩膀。

sentences.en: He's quite lucky.
sentences.zh: 他很幸运。

sentences.en: 14 of the marchers were killed.
sentences.zh: 游行者中有14人丧生。

sentences.en: So Hitler could have been killed and four policemen are killed.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒本可能被杀，还有四名警察丧生。

sentences.en: Of the leading Nazis, Göring, who'd been wounded, he goes off to exile.
sentences.zh: 在纳粹高层中，受伤的戈林流亡了。

sentences.en: He's married to a Swedish baroness or something.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一位瑞典女男爵之类的。

sentences.en: So he goes off to Sweden and becomes a morphine addict.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了瑞典，成了吗啡成瘾者。

sentences.en: That is such Göring behavior.
sentences.zh: 这太戈林了。

sentences.en: It's very Göring behavior.
sentences.zh: 这非常戈林。

sentences.en: Swedish baronesses, morphine.
sentences.zh: 瑞典女男爵，吗啡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Hitler goes off to his friend.
sentences.zh: 希特勒去找他的朋友。

sentences.en: He's got a friend called Putzi Hanfstengel, who is a sort of a useless right-wing socialite.
sentences.zh: 他有一个叫普茨·汉夫施滕格尔的朋友，是个没用的右翼社交名流。

sentences.en: He goes off to his house and he's arrested on the 11th of November.
sentences.zh: 他去了他家，并在11月11日被捕。

sentences.en: And as every biographer of Hitler says, that absolutely should have been that for Hitler.
sentences.zh: 正如希特勒的每一位传记作者所说，这对希特勒来说绝对应该是终点。

sentences.en: That should have been the end of his career, this ludicrous, shambolic, failed putsch.
sentences.zh: 这次荒谬、混乱、失败的政变本应是他职业生涯的终结。

sentences.en: However, there is another way of framing it, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 然而，还有另一种解读方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: That he had to do something like that if he was to make a successful fist of trying to gain power through legitimate democratic means.
sentences.zh: 如果他想通过合法的民主手段成功夺权，他就必须做点什么。

sentences.en: Because he had to have demonstrated that he had the courage, the balls, the Führer principle that would enable him to make a bold strike.
sentences.zh: 因为他必须证明他有勇气，有胆量，有元首原则，这使他能够进行大胆的打击。

sentences.en: And it's only having done that, that he can, you know, having demonstrated his balls, as it were, or his ball.
sentences.zh: 只有做到了这一点，他才能，你知道，展示了他的胆量，或者说他的胆子。

sentences.en: Great historical punditry there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 伟大的历史评论，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: That he can then adopt the democratic approach.
sentences.zh: 他才能采取民主路线。

sentences.en: Do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I think it's actually a very stew point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这实际上是一个非常敏锐的观点。

sentences.en: I think it means no one will ever see him as a sellout.
sentences.zh: 我认为这意味着没有人会认为他是卖国贼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, he's put his life on the line.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他把生命都押上了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: He's done what he's, you know, he has, he's risked his life for Germany.
sentences.zh: 他做了他，你知道，他确实为了德国冒了生命危险。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: I think that I hadn't thought of it that way, but that's a very astute point.
sentences.zh: 我之前没这么想过，但这是一个非常敏锐的观点。

sentences.en: That because he's done that, and the beer hall is even the beer hall itself, it becomes, that becomes, dare I say, a sacral space for the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 因为他做了这件事，甚至啤酒馆本身，它变成了，我敢说，纳粹的神圣空间。

sentences.en: Because it's, it's shambolic, it's tawdry, you know, it's pathetic in so many ways, but it provides scope for the mythologization that will happen.
sentences.zh: 因为它混乱、俗气，你知道，在很多方面都很可悲，但它为后来发生的神话化提供了空间。

sentences.en: And of course, the other thing that happens, am I not right, is that basically his trial provides him with a soapbox, because the presiding judge is a sympathizer.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一件事是，我没说错吧，基本上他的审判为他提供了一个讲坛，因为主审法官是同情者。

sentences.en: Hitler agrees to carry the can for Ludendorff, who kind of sidles off.
sentences.zh: 希特勒同意为鲁登道夫顶罪，后者悄悄溜走了。

sentences.en: And he's given this, you know, he takes the stand and just has it, you know, has a rant and makes himself into a public figure.
sentences.zh: 他被给予了，你知道，他站在被告席上，只是大发雷霆，把自己变成了一个公众人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, I'm thinking about your, your point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，我在思考你的观点。

sentences.en: Mussolini himself didn't do the march on Rome.
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼本人并没有参加向罗马进军。

sentences.en: He stayed behind, you know, in a cowardly way to see if it would work.
sentences.zh: 他留在后面，你知道，胆怯地观察是否会成功。

sentences.en: And then went by train.
sentences.zh: 然后坐火车去了。

sentences.en: Hitler actually did do this march.
sentences.zh: 希特勒确实参加了这次游行。

sentences.en: And so, and presumably that then also, I mean, all his followers know this.
sentences.zh: 所以，大概这也意味着，我是说，他所有的追随者都知道这一点。

sentences.en: Of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: He's the corporal who fought in the trenches, who then once again put his body on the line.
sentences.zh: 他是曾在战壕里战斗的下士，再次把自己的身体押上了前线。

sentences.en: Absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The trial, you make a really good point about the trial.
sentences.zh: 审判，关于审判你提到了一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: The trial should have been held in Leipzig.
sentences.zh: 审判本应在莱比锡举行。

sentences.en: The Bavarian authorities persuade the government to allow, to set up a special court in Munich,
sentences.zh: 巴伐利亚当局说服政府允许在慕尼黑设立特别法庭，

sentences.en: because basically the Bavarian authorities want to cover up their own sort of half-hearted involvement in the coup.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上巴伐利亚当局想掩盖他们自己在政变中那种三心二意的参与。

sentences.en: They make sure there's a judge who's a reactionary nationalist who's called Georg Neithart.
sentences.zh: 他们确保有一位名叫格奥尔格·奈特哈特的反动民族主义法官。

sentences.en: There's probably, we don't know, but there's probably a deal being done where Hitler says,
sentences.zh: 可能，我们不知道，但可能达成了一项交易，希特勒说，

sentences.en: I'll take all, as you said, I'll carry the can completely.
sentences.zh: 我会承担一切，正如你所说，我会完全顶罪。

sentences.en: He goes in wearing a suit, so he looks not a uniform, but he wears his iron cross to remind everybody he's a decorated war veteran.
sentences.zh: 他穿着西装进去，所以看起来不像军装，但他戴着铁十字勋章提醒大家他是一位受过勋的战争老兵。

sentences.en: And that quotation that you read out at the beginning, I mean, he's all talking about the court of history will judge me.
sentences.zh: 还有你开头读的那段引语，我是说，他一直在谈论历史法庭会审判我。

sentences.en: And he talks about it like that for four hours.
sentences.zh: 他谈论这个谈了四个小时。

sentences.en: I know, four hours.
sentences.zh: 我知道，四个小时。

sentences.en: Imagine listening to all that for four hours.
sentences.zh: 想象一下听四个小时的这些话。

sentences.en: But Hitler's speeches were incredible.
sentences.zh: 但希特勒的演讲令人难以置信。

sentences.en: They'd be like two-hour speeches normally.
sentences.zh: 通常是两个小时的演讲。

sentences.en: Hitler would not stop.
sentences.zh: 希特勒停不下来。

sentences.en: And if you've ever read, we'll get onto Mein Kampf in a second, but if you've ever read Mein Kampf, it just goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 如果你读过，我们一会儿会谈到《我的奋斗》，但如果你读过《我的奋斗》，它没完没了。

sentences.en: I mean, I know I'm not one to talk in my books.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道在我的书中我没资格说别人。

sentences.en: It's like the worst kind of podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就像最糟糕的那种播客。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, a podcast without a sort of sense of enormous self-discipline.
sentences.zh: 就像，没错，一个没有那种巨大自律感的播客。

sentences.en: Exactly, and without any breaks.
sentences.zh: 正是，而且没有任何休息。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: No ads.
sentences.zh: 没有广告。

sentences.en: No ads, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没有广告，没错。

sentences.en: So anyway, at the end of all this, Hitler is given a five-year sentence, and he is sent off to a place called Landsberg am Lech, which is an ancient kind of fortress.
sentences.zh: 总之，在这一切结束时，希特勒被判处五年监禁，并被送往一个叫莱希河畔兰茨贝格的地方，那是一座古老的堡垒。

sentences.en: And this, Ian Kershaw says, basically, it's less a prison, more a hotel, which gives you a sort of sense.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·克肖说，基本上，这与其说是监狱，不如说是酒店，这让你有一种感觉。

sentences.en: It's quite posh, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 相当高级，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's where people have been done for fighting duels in the 90th century.
sentences.zh: 那是19世纪人们因决斗而被关押的地方。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you're a duelist, you get sent to Landsberg am Lech.
sentences.zh: 没错，如果你是个决斗者，你就会被送到莱希河畔兰茨贝格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So Hitler has a big apartment there.
sentences.zh: 所以希特勒在那里有一间大公寓。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is like a hotel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那地方真的就像家酒店一样。

sentences.en: In the course of his time, so he's there for basically, what is it, a year or so?
sentences.zh: 在他待在那里的这段时间里，基本上也就是一年左右吧？

sentences.en: So the rest of it is…
sentences.zh: 剩下的时间则是……

sentences.en: So he's reading, he's reading lots of racists, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他在阅读，读了很多种族主义者的书，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Reading racists.
sentences.zh: 读种族主义者的书。

sentences.en: Reading racists.
sentences.zh: 读种族主义者的书。

sentences.en: What a hobby.
sentences.zh: 真是个好爱好。

sentences.en: What's your hobbies?
sentences.zh: 你有什么爱好？

sentences.en: So he's reading Nietzsche, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以他在读尼采吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Like you, you've read Nietzsche?
sentences.zh: 像你一样，你也读过尼采？

sentences.en: I have read Nietzsche, yes.
sentences.zh: 我确实读过尼采，是的。

sentences.en: Well, I think we should do an episode on Nietzsche and discuss how Nietzsche tends to get a clear pass from people as an influence on the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们应该做一期关于尼采的节目，讨论一下为什么人们往往会忽略尼采对纳粹的影响。

sentences.en: But I think slightly more to it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为事情没那么简单。

sentences.en: I think there is slightly more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这背后还有更深层的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 但我们之后会谈到这点。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: It may be in another episode.
sentences.zh: 也许会在另一期节目里谈。

sentences.en: But for the purpose of this, he's reading books and then he writes one.
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，他是在读书，然后写了一本书。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a Nazi supporter is a publisher called Max Amann.
sentences.zh: 当时有个纳粹支持者，是一位名叫马克斯·阿曼的出版商。

sentences.en: He says, why don't you write a book?
sentences.zh: 他建议说，你为什么不写本书呢？

sentences.en: And Hitler basically dictates his life story to two other prisoners.
sentences.zh: 于是希特勒基本上是口述了他的生平故事给另外两名囚犯记录。

sentences.en: So one of them is his chauffeur, a guy called Emil Morris.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是他的司机，一个叫埃米尔·莫里斯的人。

sentences.en: And the other is his poodle, who's Rudolf Hess.
sentences.zh: 另一个是他的跟班，也就是鲁道夫·赫斯。

sentences.en: I mean, Hess is an absolutely slavish devotee of Hitler's.
sentences.zh: 我是说，赫斯绝对是希特勒唯命是从的信徒。

sentences.en: I mean, Hitler has assembled this sort of group of cronies who think he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希特勒聚集了一群认为他才华横溢的亲信。

sentences.en: They love listening to his speeches and they will do anything for him.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢听他的演讲，并且愿意为他做任何事。

sentences.en: That's why he even has a chauffeur.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他甚至有专职司机。

sentences.en: I mean, he's living off the largesse.
sentences.zh: 他是靠慷慨的资助过活的。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, he's been living off the largesse of wealthy donors.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代，他一直靠富有的捐赠者慷慨解囊来生活。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But it's also a kind of martyrdom, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这同时也算是一种殉道，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's suffering this for the cause of Germany, for the cause of history, for these, you know, all these abstract nouns with capital letters.
sentences.zh: 他为了德国的事业，为了历史的事业，为了这些，你知道，所有这些带有大写字母的抽象名词而受苦。

sentences.en: And so the fact that he is in prison, he is a, you know, this is paradigmatic suffering, even though he's surrounded by flowers and got all these books and visitors and things.
sentences.zh: 所以他身陷囹圄的事实，这是一种典型的苦难，尽管他身边鲜花簇拥，还有那么多书、访客和各种东西。

sentences.en: So hence his struggle.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他的“奋斗”。

sentences.en: My struggle.
sentences.zh: 我的奋斗。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And so the two themes of Mein Kampf, which is the book that he writes now, one of them is a very, is the classic old Hitler theme, and it's the hatred of the Jews.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在写的这本书《我的奋斗》有两个主题，其中一个是希特勒经典的旧主题，那就是对犹太人的仇恨。

sentences.en: And he is absolutely, no one, as his biographers say, no one who read Mein Kampf could be in the slightest doubt.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常明确，正如他的传记作者所说，任何读过《我的奋斗》的人都不会有丝毫怀疑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Where there's intentions.
sentences.zh: 他的意图所在。

sentences.en: He says, you know, we will only succeed when the international poisons are exterminated.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，只有当国际毒素被清除时，我们才会成功。

sentences.en: And he refers to them again and again as a virus, as maggots, as a pestilence, as a plague.
sentences.zh: 他反复提到他们是病毒、蛆虫、瘟疫、灾祸。

sentences.en: He talks of annihilating, expelling, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他谈论着消灭、驱逐，所有这些类似的事情。

sentences.en: The other thing that is more new, however, is the obsession now with Russia.
sentences.zh: 然而，另一个更新的东西，是他现在对俄国的痴迷。

sentences.en: So you don't see that at the beginning, the obsession with Marxism and with Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以你在最开始看不到这一点，即对马克思主义和俄国的痴迷。

sentences.en: But now he's talking about the end of Russia as a state, about Russia being given over to the German plow.
sentences.zh: 但现在他在谈论作为国家的俄国的终结，谈论将俄国交给德国的犁去耕耘。

sentences.en: So this sort of labens ram idea.
sentences.zh: 也就是这种“生存空间”的理念。

sentences.en: And as Richard Evans says, no one who reads this can think that Hitler is just about revising the Treaty of Versailles.
sentences.zh: 正如理查德·埃文斯所说，任何读过这本书的人都不会认为希特勒只是想修改《凡尔赛条约》。

sentences.en: Hitler is also about building a new empire in the East, about killing Jews, about turning Slavs into helots and slaves,
sentences.zh: 希特勒还意在东方建立一个新的帝国，屠杀犹太人，把斯拉夫人变成农奴和奴隶，

sentences.en: and giving Germans living space in the steppes.
sentences.zh: 并为德国人在草原上提供生存空间。

sentences.en: And before he goes in, before he goes in, you described him as John the Baptist, and he was obviously playing second fiddle to Ludendorff.
sentences.zh: 在你进去之前，你曾形容他是施洗约翰，而且他显然是在给鲁登道夫打下手。

sentences.en: But does his experience in prison, his process of self-reflection, the idolization he's getting from all his various followers,
sentences.zh: 但他在监狱里的经历，他的自我反思过程，他从各种追随者那里得到的偶像化崇拜，

sentences.en: is this when he starts to think that perhaps he is the man destined to be the leader, the Fuhrer?
sentences.zh: 这是他开始认为自己或许就是命中注定的领袖——元首的时候吗？

sentences.en: I think absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我觉得绝对是。

sentences.en: I think when he comes out of Landsberg Amlech, he undoubtedly thinks of himself as the leader now.
sentences.zh: 我认为当他走出莱希河畔兰茨贝格时，他无疑已经把自己视为领袖了。

sentences.en: There's something about that experience of maybe the putsch, but then the experience of being on trial and being the martyr,
sentences.zh: 那次经历，也许是政变，但随后是受审并成为烈士的经历，

sentences.en: and then having these 500 guests with flowers and racist books that has puffed him up.
sentences.zh: 再加上有500名带着鲜花和种族主义书籍的访客，这让他变得膨胀了。

sentences.en: And he thinks, I'm the man of destiny.
sentences.zh: 他想，我是天选之人。

sentences.en: And so this is why when he comes out, he gets everyone to, he basically refans the Nazi party, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么他出来后，让每个人，他基本上重组了纳粹党，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he gets everyone to sign, you know, to swear an unconditional oath to him.
sentences.zh: 他让每个人都签字，你知道，向他宣誓效忠。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: It's an extraordinary scene.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非凡的场景。

sentences.en: Ian Kershaw says, like, medieval vassals swearing undying loyalty to the leader.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·克肖说，就像中世纪的附庸向领主宣誓效忠一样。

sentences.en: I mean, they pledge themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们向他承诺。

sentences.en: They pledge fealty to him.
sentences.zh: 他们向他宣誓效忠。

sentences.en: And so this is when you start getting the Harl Hitler and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你开始听到“希特勒万岁”以及诸如此类东西的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So much more of that.
sentences.zh: 多得多了。

sentences.en: Of course, that's slightly copied on the sort of, he's inherited it from Schoenner, who we talked about in the first podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，这稍微有点模仿，他是从我们在第一期播客中谈到的舍内雷尔那里继承来的。

sentences.en: But it's also all to do with that stuff about knights and a brotherhood.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也与骑士和兄弟会的那套东西有关。

sentences.en: And of course, it's also to do with Mussolini and fascism and all the rituals of fascism.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也与墨索里尼、法西斯主义以及法西斯主义的所有仪式有关。

sentences.en: All these things, these influences flow together to create this Fuhrer cult.
sentences.zh: 所有这些影响汇聚在一起，创造了这个“元首崇拜”。

sentences.en: And actually, the Fuhrer cult, which seems ludicrous to us and sinister,
sentences.zh: 实际上，这个在我们看来既荒谬又阴险的元首崇拜，

sentences.en: Ian Kershaw says it's really important because the Nazis had always been slightly, you know, they'd all been different factions.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·克肖说这非常重要，因为纳粹一直以来都有点，你知道，他们一直都是不同的派系。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, because it's inherently vociferous, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为这本质上就是吵吵闹闹的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, everyone knows this about kind of eccentric political sects on the fringes, that they're always splitting up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家都知道边缘政治派别总是这样，他们总是分裂。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the whole Judean People's Front joke.
sentences.zh: 就像那个“犹太人民阵线”的笑话一样。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: But now that they've basically sworn their loyalty to the Fuhrer, to the leader,
sentences.zh: 但现在他们基本上已经向元首宣誓效忠了，

sentences.en: factionalism, it doesn't come to an end.
sentences.zh: 派系斗争并没有结束。

sentences.en: Of course, there'll be more factionalism to come.
sentences.zh: 当然，未来还会有更多的派系斗争。

sentences.en: But there's a kind of coherence there.
sentences.zh: 但其中有一种连贯性。

sentences.en: This is the message.
sentences.zh: 这就是核心信息。

sentences.en: This is the guy.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个人。

sentences.en: End of story.
sentences.zh: 故事结束。

sentences.en: But isn't there also...
sentences.zh: 但难道没有……

sentences.en: We're walking with destiny.
sentences.zh: 我们正与命运同行。

sentences.en: Something else that Hitler has got from this is this idea that there can be no march on Berlin because it hasn't worked, it won't work.
sentences.zh: 希特勒从中学到的另一件事是，不可能有“进军柏林”这种事，因为它没用，也不会奏效。

sentences.en: And therefore, there's this idea that he will destroy democracy through democratic means.
sentences.zh: 因此，他有了通过民主手段摧毁民主的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're absolutely right, which is a chilling thing and has been a chilling thing ever since.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你说得完全正确，这令人不寒而栗，而且从那时起一直令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Well, that's what makes him so unsettling for people living in a democracy to this day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么直到今天，他对于生活在民主国家的人来说仍然如此令人不安。

sentences.en: That all democracies have to contend with.
sentences.zh: 这是所有民主国家都必须面对的。

sentences.en: That what happens when you have somebody who doesn't play by the rules?
sentences.zh: 当有人不按规则出牌时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so what is the state of the Weimar democracy by this point?
sentences.zh: 那么魏玛民主在此时处于什么状态？

sentences.en: So what, kind of early 1925?
sentences.zh: 大概是1925年初？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So now we have a series of steps.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有一系列步骤。

sentences.en: We're going to have them in the last few minutes of this podcast and then particularly in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本期播客的最后几分钟，以及下一期节目中详细讨论。

sentences.en: A series of steps whereby the guardians of the Weimar Republic, the very people who should be protecting it, start to dismantle it.
sentences.zh: 魏玛共和国的守护者们，那些本应保护它的人，开始拆解它的一系列步骤。

sentences.en: Start to sign, in some cases, to sign their own death warrants.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，开始签署他们自己的死亡判决书。

sentences.en: The first moment, it's bad luck.
sentences.zh: 第一个时刻，是坏运气。

sentences.en: It's really bad luck.
sentences.zh: 真是倒霉。

sentences.en: Friedrich Ebert, the president, the guy who was synonymous with Weimar.
sentences.zh: 弗里德里希·艾伯特，总统，那个魏玛的代名词。

sentences.en: So the Clement Attlee of Weimar.
sentences.zh: 也就是魏玛的克莱门特·艾德礼。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Clement Attlee, as I described him.
sentences.zh: 正如我所描述的，克莱门特·艾德礼。

sentences.en: He dies of appendicitis.
sentences.zh: 他死于阑尾炎。

sentences.en: He's neglected it too long.
sentences.zh: 他拖得太久没去管它。

sentences.en: He's under tremendous pressure, horrendous abuse in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 他承受着巨大的压力，报纸上对他进行了可怕的辱骂。

sentences.en: He neglects it.
sentences.zh: 他忽视了病情。

sentences.en: He dies of appendicitis.
sentences.zh: 他死于阑尾炎。

sentences.en: This is a disaster for Weimar.
sentences.zh: 这对魏玛来说是一场灾难。

sentences.en: They then have a presidential election.
sentences.zh: 他们随后举行了总统选举。

sentences.en: Ludendorff actually runs.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫实际上参选了。

sentences.en: He gets 1%.
sentences.zh: 他只得了1%的选票。

sentences.en: That's pretty badly.
sentences.zh: 那真是太惨了。

sentences.en: That's the end of him.
sentences.zh: 那是他的终点。

sentences.en: But his partner in the First World War, his sort of dictatorial partner, Paul von Hindenburg, who is this sort of – he looks like he's been chiseled out of a massive Prussian –
sentences.zh: 但他一战时的搭档，那种独裁式的伙伴，保罗·冯·兴登堡，他看起来就像是从一块巨大的普鲁士——

sentences.en: Prussian walrus.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士海象。

sentences.en: Yeah, Prussian walrus.
sentences.zh: 是啊，普鲁士海象。

sentences.en: Massive moustache.
sentences.zh: 巨大的胡子。

sentences.en: Giant head.
sentences.zh: 巨大的脑袋。

sentences.en: I imagine he wears a helmet with a spike in the bath.
sentences.zh: 我能想象他洗澡时戴着带尖刺的头盔。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's like a square man who's been cut out of wood.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他就像一个木头雕刻出来的方块人。

sentences.en: Very reactionary, very monarchist, doesn't really believe in Weimar.
sentences.zh: 非常反动，非常保皇，并不真正相信魏玛。

sentences.en: He actually seeks permission from the Kaiser before he throws his hat in the presidential ring.
sentences.zh: 他在投身总统竞选之前，实际上还征求了德皇的许可。

sentences.en: He doesn't even run the first round.
sentences.zh: 他甚至没有参加第一轮投票。

sentences.en: He's co-operative, runs in the second round.
sentences.zh: 他很配合，参加了第二轮。

sentences.en: He's 78 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时78岁。

sentences.en: He becomes the president of Germany.
sentences.zh: 他成为了德国总统。

sentences.en: And he and his circle, so he's surrounded by kind of cronies, particularly army advisors.
sentences.zh: 他和他的圈子，他被一群亲信包围着，特别是军队顾问。

sentences.en: None of them are keen on democracy.
sentences.zh: 他们没人喜欢民主。

sentences.en: None of them are keen on Weimar.
sentences.zh: 他们没人喜欢魏玛。

sentences.en: They're basically itching to destroy it.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上迫不及待地想摧毁它。

sentences.en: That is a disaster for Weimar.
sentences.zh: 这对魏玛来说是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Nazis – so these are the supposedly the golden years of the Weimar Republic, the last years, because the inflation is over.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纳粹——这些被认为是魏玛共和国的黄金岁月，最后几年，因为通货膨胀结束了。

sentences.en: The economy is doing a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 经济状况稍微好了一些。

sentences.en: The Nazi party is actually, although it's very small, it's beginning to grow.
sentences.zh: 纳粹党实际上，虽然规模很小，但开始壮大了。

sentences.en: And the key thing that it does is that it moves out.
sentences.zh: 而它所做的关键事情是向外扩张。

sentences.en: So it's been in Munich, in Bavaria, which is very, very, as you all know, Tom, very, very Catholic.
sentences.zh: 所以它之前一直在慕尼黑，在巴伐利亚，正如你们所知，汤姆，那里非常非常天主教化。

sentences.en: And where institutionally there's a lot of kind of – there's an obvious resistance to Hitler's message because the Catholic Church is very strong.
sentences.zh: 而且在制度上，由于天主教会势力强大，对希特勒的信息有着明显的抵制。

sentences.en: Well, because Munich is a kind of – it's an island of political turbulence surrounded by Catholic peasantry, basically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为慕尼黑基本上是一个被天主教农民包围的政治动荡孤岛。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what they start to do is to build support in the Protestant north of Germany.
sentences.zh: 但他们开始做的是在德国新教徒占多数的北部地区建立支持。

sentences.en: Which they have to do, don't they, if they're going to become national, because there are far more Protestants in Germany than Catholics.
sentences.zh: 他们必须这样做，不是吗？如果他们想成为全国性的政党，因为德国的新教徒远多于天主教徒。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 同意。

sentences.en: There's a key figure here is a man called Gregor Strasser.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个关键人物，名叫格雷戈尔·斯特拉瑟。

sentences.en: He's sort of Hitler's ideological rival, if you like, in the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，他算是希特勒在纳粹党内的意识形态对手。

sentences.en: He's the other guy who's clever.
sentences.zh: 他是另一个聪明人。

sentences.en: He's certainly cleverer than – Not in the long run a good thing to be an ideological rival to Hitler in the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 他当然比——从长远来看，在纳粹党内做希特勒的意识形态对手可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没错。

sentences.en: He's a brilliant organiser.
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的组织者。

sentences.en: He's a brilliant administrator.
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的行政管理者。

sentences.en: He's been sort of building it up while Hitler was in prison.
sentences.zh: 在希特勒入狱期间，他一直在经营这个党。

sentences.en: And when he goes around North Germany, Strasser, he emphasises the socialism as well as the national.
sentences.zh: 当斯特拉瑟在德国北部四处奔走时，他不仅强调民族主义，还强调社会主义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he talks to industrial working – because it's very industrial in North Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以他与工业工人阶级对话——因为德国北部工业非常发达。

sentences.en: And he talks to people there and he says, you know, we'll do – you'll have higher wages, you'll have better living standards, we'll protect your working conditions, all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他与那里的人们交谈，他说，你知道，我们会做到的——你们会有更高的工资，更好的生活水平，我们会保护你们的工作条件，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So he's the guy really who brings in Goebbels, Joseph Goebbels.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实是把戈培尔，也就是约瑟夫·戈培尔带进来的人。

sentences.en: Goebbels is from the industrial Rhineland.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔来自工业化的莱茵兰地区。

sentences.en: He's a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: He is a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他确实是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He has a PhD from Heidelberg on romantic drama.
sentences.zh: 他拥有海德堡大学浪漫主义戏剧专业的博士学位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What do you believe?
sentences.zh: 你相信吗？

sentences.en: I didn't know what Goebbels was a doctor of and it seems very implausible.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道戈培尔是哪个专业的博士，这听起来很不真实。

sentences.en: But he's quite bohemian, Goebbels.
sentences.zh: 但戈培尔确实相当波西米亚风。

sentences.en: And he'd actually been drawn to the far left and the far right.
sentences.zh: 他实际上曾被极左和极右思想所吸引。

sentences.en: He'd read Marx.
sentences.zh: 他读过马克思的著作。

sentences.en: He gets in with Strasser.
sentences.zh: 他与斯特拉瑟混在一起。

sentences.en: He's a regular propagandiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是个地道的宣传家。

sentences.en: So, I mean, people say two things about Goebbels' sense of theatrical.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，人们对戈培尔的戏剧感有两种评价。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you say romantic drama.
sentences.zh: 而你提到了浪漫主义戏剧。

sentences.en: Firstly, that he's Catholic.
sentences.zh: 首先，他是天主教徒。

sentences.en: So there's the sense of the, you know, the church display and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种，你知道，教会展示以及所有这类东西的感觉。

sentences.en: But secondly, precisely that he is – he comes from this theatrical milieu.
sentences.zh: 但其次，恰恰因为他——他来自这种戏剧圈子。

sentences.en: That he – in a sense, the Nazis end up making Germany a stage for incredible pageantry and swagger.
sentences.zh: 他——从某种意义上说，纳粹最终把德国变成了一个充满不可思议的盛大排场和傲慢姿态的舞台。

sentences.en: And that is obviously part of the appeal of the Nazis is that, you know, they're not boring in terms of their projection.
sentences.zh: 显然，纳粹吸引力的一部分就在于，你知道，他们在形象展示方面一点也不无聊。

sentences.en: And Goebbels is brilliant at that.
sentences.zh: 而戈培尔在这方面非常出色。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Of course, you really need to watch Triumph of the Will, Lenny Riefenstahl's film, to know that they're not boring.
sentences.zh: 当然，你真的需要看看莱尼·里芬斯塔尔拍摄的电影《意志的胜利》，才能知道他们并不无聊。

sentences.en: But what Strasser and Goebbels do, they're very good at broadening its appeal to actually quite boring people.
sentences.zh: 但斯特拉瑟和戈培尔所做的是，他们非常擅长将这种吸引力扩大到那些实际上相当无聊的人群中。

sentences.en: So particularly farmers, the sort of people in the countryside in North Germany.
sentences.zh: 特别是农民，也就是德国北部乡村地区的那类人。

sentences.en: There's an agricultural depression.
sentences.zh: 当时正处于农业萧条期。

sentences.en: But Goebbels goes to Berlin, though, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但戈培尔后来去了柏林，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he becomes the galleiter in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 所以他成了柏林的大区长。

sentences.en: Yeah, but much later on.
sentences.zh: 是的，但那是很久以后的事了。

sentences.en: That's later, is it?
sentences.zh: 那是后来才发生的，是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At the moment, he's sort of torn between Strasser and Hitler a little bit.
sentences.zh: 当时，他在斯特拉瑟和希特勒之间稍微有点摇摆不定。

sentences.en: But what they're doing, they're launching recruiting drives in these sort of rural places, Schleswig-Holstein, Oldenburg.
sentences.zh: 但他们正在做的是，在石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因、奥尔登堡这些农村地区发起招募活动。

sentences.en: So even though they do really badly, generally, the Nazis, in the 1928 Reichstag elections, they win less than 3% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管纳粹在1928年的国会选举中表现非常糟糕，得票率不到3%。

sentences.en: They only get 12 deputies.
sentences.zh: 他们只获得了12个议席。

sentences.en: Strasser is one.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉瑟是一个。

sentences.en: Goebbels is one.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔是一个。

sentences.en: Goering is one.
sentences.zh: 戈林是一个。

sentences.en: They're actually doing better and better in these kind of Protestant agricultural regions.
sentences.zh: 但他们在这些新教农业地区实际上表现得越来越好。

sentences.en: So what are they offering?
sentences.zh: 那么他们提供了什么？

sentences.en: What's the pitch?
sentences.zh: 他们的卖点是什么？

sentences.en: So the pitch is, the pitch is, we will listen to you and nobody else is listening.
sentences.zh: 卖点就是，卖点就是，我们会倾听你们的声音，而其他人都不听。

sentences.en: I mean, the Social Democrats are a city party.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，社会民主党是一个城市政党。

sentences.en: They're nationalists, the right-wing party.
sentences.zh: 他们是民族主义者，是右翼政党。

sentences.en: They are a bigwigs establishment, rich people's party, middle-class party.
sentences.zh: 他们是权贵阶层、富人政党、中产阶级政党。

sentences.en: The Nazis are saying, they're rebranding themselves as a genuinely national party with something for everybody, and particularly for those who've been left behind.
sentences.zh: 纳粹则在说，他们正在重塑自己，成为一个真正的民族政党，为每个人提供一些东西，特别是为那些被遗忘的人。

sentences.en: And the sort of Protestant countryside feels like it has been left behind.
sentences.zh: 而新教乡村地区感觉自己被遗忘了。

sentences.en: They say, we'll set up farmers, cooperatives.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们会建立农民合作社。

sentences.en: We'll take farmers seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们会认真对待农民。

sentences.en: So they are reaching out to farmers and people like them, craftsmen, artisans, shopkeepers, the self-employed.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在向农民和像他们一样的人伸出援手，比如工匠、手艺人、店主、个体经营者。

sentences.en: And they're saying, you know, we'll make Germany great again.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，我们会让德国再次伟大。

sentences.en: We'll listen to you.
sentences.zh: 我们会倾听你们的声音。

sentences.en: We'll put the economy on an even keel.
sentences.zh: 我们会让经济重回正轨。

sentences.en: You'll be better paid.
sentences.zh: 你们会得到更好的报酬。

sentences.en: But you'll feel proud to be German again.
sentences.zh: 但你们会再次为身为德国人而感到自豪。

sentences.en: No one feels proud to be German anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在已经没有人为身为德国人而感到自豪了。

sentences.en: They particularly have a strong appeal, by the way, to young people.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们对年轻人特别有吸引力。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if you're young, if you didn't live through – if you didn't fight in the First World War,
sentences.zh: 因为当然，如果你很年轻，如果你没有经历过——如果你没有参加过第一次世界大战，

sentences.en: you have a slight sense of guilt and you wish you'd done it, you missed out on it.
sentences.zh: 你会有一种轻微的负罪感，你希望自己参加过，你错过了它。

sentences.en: But you've also been through crisis after crisis.
sentences.zh: 但你也经历了一次又一次的危机。

sentences.en: A good example of that is a young man, a bright young man who was born in Munich.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是一个年轻人，一个出生在慕尼黑的聪明年轻人。

sentences.en: His father was a Catholic schoolteacher who was born in 1900, never got to see action in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一位天主教学校老师，他出生于1900年，从未在第一次世界大战中上过战场。

sentences.en: Clever, studded after the First World War, sucked into the far-right scene.
sentences.zh: 他很聪明，一战后开始学习，被卷入了极右翼圈子。

sentences.en: And he's Heinrich Himmler.
sentences.zh: 他就是海因里希·希姆莱。

sentences.en: So Himmler, I mean, who most of us would regard as one of the most sinister men who's ever lived, he joined the Nazi Party in 1925.
sentences.zh: 所以希姆莱，我的意思是，我们大多数人会认为他是史上最邪恶的人之一，他在1925年加入了纳粹党。

sentences.en: He hero-worships Hitler.
sentences.zh: 他把希特勒奉为英雄。

sentences.en: I mean, Himmler brings to the table all of these enthusiasms, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希姆莱带来了所有这些狂热，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or all the kind of mad occult stuff and everything.
sentences.zh: 或者所有那些疯狂的神秘学之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, herbalism, the Thule Society, runes, all of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，草药学、图勒协会、卢恩字母，所有这些。

sentences.en: And also very, very radical racism.
sentences.zh: 还有非常、非常激进的种族主义。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems weird to say this as such a wicked man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说一个如此邪恶的人有理想主义，这听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: There is an idealism to Himmler.
sentences.zh: 希姆莱确实有一种理想主义。

sentences.en: I mean, he worships Hitler.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他崇拜希特勒。

sentences.en: He thinks as a young man, he thinks this is the route to the utopia.
sentences.zh: 他年轻时认为，这就是通往乌托邦的道路。

sentences.en: This is – everything is rubbish and tawdry.
sentences.zh: 这就是——一切都是垃圾和廉价货。

sentences.en: Of course, of course, because the Nazis don't see themselves as evil.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然，因为纳粹并不认为自己是邪恶的。

sentences.en: The Nazis see themselves doing what is right for Germany and for their race.
sentences.zh: 纳粹认为他们是在为德国和他们的种族做正确的事。

sentences.en: And you have to make that leap of trying to see them as they see themselves, or else you won't understand the nature of their appeal.
sentences.zh: 你必须跨出这一步，试着像他们看待自己那样看待他们，否则你就无法理解他们吸引力的本质。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they don't see themselves as wicked.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并不认为自己是邪恶的。

sentences.en: No, they don't even see – I mean, certainly they don't see their anti-Semitism as wicked.
sentences.zh: 不，他们甚至不认为——我的意思是，他们当然不认为他们的反犹主义是邪恶的。

sentences.en: No, because they see it as being for the good of the German people.
sentences.zh: 不，因为他们认为这是为了德国人民的利益。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, of course, at this point, they are small.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在这一点上，他们还很弱小。

sentences.en: They're still a fringe party.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然是一个边缘政党。

sentences.en: They are growing in these sort of Protestant rural areas, but they're still a long way from being a major party.
sentences.zh: 他们在这些新教农村地区正在成长，但距离成为大党还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: I mean, the big parties are in a grand coalition, actually, the Social Democrats, the Catholic Center Party, and the Liberal Democrats Party.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大党实际上正处于大联合政府中，即社会民主党、天主教中央党和自由民主党。

sentences.en: And there's no reason at that point, nobody in sort of 1928 or so,
sentences.zh: 在那一点上没有任何理由，在1928年左右，没有人

sentences.en: seriously thinks that within five years, the Nazis will be the masters.
sentences.zh: 会认真认为五年内纳粹就会成为主人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, shall we leave today's episode with a passage from Richard Evans?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们用理查德·埃文斯的一段话来结束今天的节目，好吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, go for it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好的，开始吧，汤姆。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It would need a catastrophe of major dimensions if an extremist party like the Nazis was to gain mass support.
sentences.zh: 如果像纳粹这样的极端政党要获得群众支持，就需要一场大规模的灾难。

sentences.en: In 1929, with the sudden collapse of the economy in the wake of the stock exchange crash in New York, it came.
sentences.zh: 1929年，随着纽约股市崩盘引发的经济突然崩溃，灾难降临了。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
